title: Join two rectangular duct sections and lock the joint with a drive cleat on each side
instruction: Join the loose duct section to the fixed one and lock the joint with the two drive cleats, then let go.
context: Sheet metal workers (O*NET 47-2211.00) and HVAC installers (49-9021.00) join rectangular duct with S-and-drive slips: the next section goes under the S-slip with its side flanges back to back with the fixed section's, then a drive cleat is slid down over each flange pair. A drive put on over a gap or a skewed joint leaks. Unlike TK-V2QDW6 and TK-42VCGC (a sleeve slid along pipe ends), this task squares a part into a joint and clips across it from above.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: 'in front' is away from the arms, 'left' is the robot's left; heights are above the table top. All duct is galvanised steel, 1.6 mm sheet, rectangular, 120 mm wide, 40 mm tall and 120 mm long, open at both ends, its length front to back. Fixed section: 34.0 to 46.0 cm in front, centred on the midline, its open near end at 34.0 cm. At that end a dark grey 2 mm flange stands 15 mm out from each side, full height, and a dark S-slip lip 10 mm long, 120 mm wide and 4 mm thick runs over the top sheet, its underside 1.5 mm above it, reaching to 33.0 cm; the loose section's top sheet must pass under it. Loose section (150 g): the same, with matching dark grey flanges at its far end and a dark grip bar (20 mm front to back, 40 mm wide, 15 mm tall) on the middle of its top; its centre starts 22.0 cm in front and 2.5 cm left, turned 8 deg so its far end points left of straight ahead. Two loose drive cleats (bright orange steel, 30 g): channels 55 mm tall, 24 mm front to back and 20 mm across, with an 8 mm wide, 12 mm deep slot down their full height; over the bottom 4 mm each cheek is set 2.5 mm further out (a 13 mm lead-in, the cleat 29 mm front to back there). The two are mirror images, so either fits either side turned round. They stand upright at 27.0 cm in front, 15.0 cm left and 15.0 cm right of the midline, slots facing the midline. Nothing else is on the table. Lot B: the loose section starts 2.5 cm right instead, turned 8 deg the other way. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, a feeler gauge and a top photo. Home: at each side's flange pair, the loose flange within 1 mm of the fixed one (gap under 1 mm, measured at the middle of the flange); the loose section's centre line within 2 mm of the fixed one's, within 1.5 deg of square and tilted under 1.5 deg, lying flat on the table (lowest point within 1.5 mm). A flange pair has a cleat on when either cleat stands upright (within 5 deg) with its slot facing the duct (within 10 deg), its bottom within 3 mm of the table, both flanges inside its 8 mm slot (not just the lead-in) and at least 5 mm of them in it; one cleat counts for one pair. Released and still: no part of either gripper within 5 mm of the section or a cleat, none of them moving. 1.0: home, both pairs cleated. 0.6: home, one pair. 0.25: home, no cleat on. Every tier needs released and still; 0 otherwise, including a section short, off centre, skewed, tilted or held. Scored at the last step, or 1.0 once held for 1.5 s. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Stand both cleats back upright on their marks with their slots facing the midline, and set the loose section back on its marks for the lot: lot A 2.5 cm left and turned 8 deg (far end to the left), lot B 2.5 cm right and turned 8 deg the other way. The fixed section, its flanges and lip do not move. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: About 1:3 scale, rigid boxes, default friction (1.2/1.0). Only the top S-slip is modelled, as a fixed lip. The 8 mm slot is looser than a real drive on two 2 mm flanges, so the 1 mm gap is enforced by the scorer; real drives are hammered on and their ends bent over, here they slide or are pressed down. The lead-in is a step, not a flare. Two lots stop a fixed shift or turn, not a memorised replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
